title: Integrated randomization norm bound
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, and let $f,g$ be real-valued functions on its outcome space. If $q>0$, $A\ge0$, and for every outcome $x$ the uniform-cube power mean of $r\mapsto R_rf(x)$ is at most $A$ times that of $r\mapsto R_rg(x)$, then the joint power mean over product outcomes and uniform cube points satisfies $\|Rf\|_q\le A\|Rg\|_q$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses
$f,g$ are real-valued functions on the product outcome space
For every product outcome, the stated pointwise uniform-cube power-mean bound holds
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f,g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, $q>0$, and $A\ge0$. If $\|r\mapsto R_rf(x)\|_q\le A\|r\mapsto R_rg(x)\|_q$ on the uniform sign cube for every $x$, then $\|Rf\|_q\le A\|Rg\|_q$, where $\|Rh\|_q=(\mathbb E_{x\sim P}\mathbb E_r|R_rh(x)|^q)^{1/q}$.
